newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU mulls more ambitious role for Europol.
newsitem.headline: EU mulls more ambitious role for Europol.

text.p: European Union justice ministers on Wednesday discussed giving a more ambitious role to the bloc's embryonic police agency Europol, even before it is fully operational.

But as ministers dreamt up new tasks for the Hague-based agency they were warned that unless they urgently ratified crime fighting conventions already on the table they would be fighting a losing battle against organised crime.

"If you don't do this the criminals will find the countries with the loopholes which will help them get away," the EU's Justice Commissioner Anita Gradin told a news conference after the first day of a two-day meeting.

With only Britain out of the 15 EU members having ratified the convention which will put Europol fully to work, ministers floated ideas like involving police officers from eastern Europe, fast becoming a haven for crime rings.
As police tighten the net in the west, the east is becoming a prime location for making designer drugs like ecstasy.

Dutch Justice Minister Winnie Sorgdrager said EU countries acknowledged they had to tighten cooperation among police, customs and judicial authorities to effectively fight crime from drugs to money laundering.
While police cooperation is blossoming, criminals can still benefit from lax checks at airports and harbours, Gradin said.
Conventions on customs cooperation, extradition and fraud have not been ratified by a single EU country.
Sorgdrager said the Netherlands, which as EU president hosted the meeting, was pressuring member states to ratify the Europol convention by the year-end.

Sorgdrager played down talk that Europol would eventually move towards being a European version of the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), saying the idea had been exaggerated after EU leaders met at the end of last year.
